phase.text: A single registration efficacy and safety trial

citations.quote: data from a single registration efficacy and safety trial in four patients with HOA (Protocol 401.13.001)

design.text: A 6-week open-label efficacy and safety trial followed by an extension trial of unspecified length, conducted at two US sites

citations.quote: This was a 6-week open-label efficacy and safety trial followed by an extension trial (length unspecified). The target enrollment for the trial was 4 to 10 patients with HOA.

population.text: Patients with hereditary orotic aciduria aged ≤19 years (3 previously treated with uridine, 1 treatment-naive), age range 3 to 19 years

citations.quote: The efficacy of XURIDEN was evaluated in an open-label study in 4 patients with hereditary orotic aciduria (3 male, 1 female; age range from 3 to 19 years). Three patients were previously treated with uridine and were switched at study entry to XURIDEN. All patients were administered XURIDEN orally at a daily dosage of 60 mg/kg once daily. The study duration was 6 weeks.

endpoint.text: Stability (for patients switching from uridine) or improvement (for the treatment-naive patient) of patient-specific predetermined hematologic parameters (neutrophil count, white blood cell count, or mean corpuscular volume) at Days 28 and 42

citations.quote: For patients switching from oral uridine to oral uridine triacetate, the primary efficacy endpoint was stability of pre-determined hematologic parameters (neutrophil count, white blood cell count, or mean corpuscular volume) individualized by patient. Stability was defined as:
For patients not previously treated with uridine, stability was defined as improvement in an abnormal baseline value or worsening no more than 15% to 30% at Days 28 and 42.

n.text: 4 patients (all 4 completed the main treatment phase)

citations.quote: Study 001 was conducted in four patients, including 3 patients who were previously treated with uridine and one treatment-naïve patient
All four patients completed the main treatment phase of the trial and are continuing treatment in the extension phase.

result.text: All three patients who transitioned from uridine maintained stable hematologic parameters after 6 weeks; no improvement in hematologic status was demonstrated in the treatment-naive patient. Hematologic parameters for all four patients continued to show stability or improvement during the 6-month extension period.

indication.text: XURIDEN is indicated for the treatment of hereditary orotic aciduria.

target_moa.text: Uridine triacetate is a pro-drug of uridine that forms uridine upon metabolism, providing uridine in the systemic circulation of patients with hereditary orotic aciduria (UMP synthase deficiency) who cannot synthesize adequate uridine; restoration of intracellular uridine nucleotides reduces overproduction of orotic acid by feedback inhibition.

citations.quote: Uridine triacetate is a pro-drug of uridine that forms uridine and free acetate upon metabolism (see Figure 2).

XURIDEN provides uridine in the systemic circulation of patients with hereditary orotic aciduria who cannot synthesize adequate quantities of uridine due to a genetic defect in uridine nucleotide synthesis.
When intracellular uridine nucleotides are restored into the normal range, overproduction of orotic acid is reduced by feedback inhibition, so that urinary excretion of orotic acid

modality.text: Small molecule (pyrimidine analog / pro-drug of uridine)

citations.quote: XURIDEN is a pyrimidine analog for uridine replacement indicated for the treatment of hereditary orotic aciduria. (1)
Uridine triacetate is a pro-drug of uridine that forms uridine and free acetate upon metabolism (see Figure 2).

key_safety.text: No adverse reactions were reported with XURIDEN. Safety was assessed in 4 patients with hereditary orotic aciduria (ages 3 to 19 years) receiving 60 mg/kg once daily for six weeks and continuing at up to 120 mg/kg once daily for at least 9 months.

citations.quote: The safety of XURIDEN was assessed in 4 patients with hereditary orotic aciduria ranging in age from 3 to 19 years (3 male, 1 female) who received 60 mg/kg of XURIDEN once daily for six weeks. The patients continued to receive XURIDEN for at least 9 months at dosages of up to 120 mg/kg once daily. No adverse reactions were reported with XURIDEN.

The extension trial should collect data on growth, hematologic indices, and urine biomarkers (orotic acid and orotidine). Growth data should include height, weight, height velocity and weight

requirement.text: 2932-2: Develop a discriminating dissolution method, set acceptance criteria based on at least 5 commercial batches, determine particle size distribution of the final drug product and evaluate its impact on dissolution, and update the final drug product particle size specification and in-process controls.

citations.quote: 2932-2 Develop a discriminating dissolution method appropriate for the proposed product and set dissolution method acceptance criteria based on data from at least 5 commercial batches. Determine the particle size distribution of the final drug product and, using the updated dissolution method, evaluate the impact of the particle size distribution on dissolution. The studies should also include an evaluation of batches submitted in the application (e.g., W017891, W017893, W017895, W012785, and W021129). Based on findings from these studies, update the final drug product particle size specification and the in-process controls.

orphan_indication.text: Uridine triacetate was granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of hereditary orotic aciduria (Orphan Product designation granted August 9, 2014).

citations.quote: Uridine triacetate was granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of hereditary orotic aciduria. Therefore, this application is exempt from the requirements of the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA).
**August 9, 2014:** The Agency granted Orphan Product designation for uridine triacetate for HOA.

summary.text: Xuriden (uridine triacetate) for hereditary orotic aciduria received Breakthrough Product designation (April 25, 2014) and Orphan Product designation (August 9, 2014). The NDA, received January 8, 2015, was approved September 4, 2015 based on a single open-label registration trial in 4 patients, with the sponsor granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.

citations.quote: **April 25, 2014:** The Agency granted Breakthrough Product designation for uridine triacetate for HOA based on clinical data presented from published case studies and clinical summaries for the expanded access INDs.
**August 9, 2014:** The Agency granted Orphan Product designation for uridine triacetate for HOA.

We also inform you that you have been granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, as provided under section 529 of the FDCA. This priority review voucher (PRV) has been assigned a tracking number, PRV NDA 208169. All correspondences related to this voucher should refer to this tracking number.
